The numbers for "Monopoly 200X" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
696.headline: The prize table, line by line

762.body:
The top prize count on "Billion" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of four top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

If you play "Billion" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
762.headline: Over a month, no top prize claimed

827.body:
"50th Anniversary" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of its unclaimed prize money, about two-thirds is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

For "50th Anniversary" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Everything above about "50th Anniversary" comes from the Ohio Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
827.headline: How the prize money is divided

847.body:

847.headline: No $500,000 prize is left

891.body:
The most common win left on "Cash Explosion 25X" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Every line of Cash Explosion 25X's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
